Job Description

We are looking for a passionate, action-oriented, and communicative senior data security professional with exceptional problem-solving skills, drive, and self-motivation to join the Data Security team, reporting to the Global Head of Security at Alter Domus. The incumbent will work alongside a geographically diverse team of security professionals focusing on setting up our Data Security Posture Management program and DLP controls.

A Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) and Data Loss Prevention (DLP) analyst secures an organization's sensitive information across its entire digital ecosystem. This role combines proactive risk assessment (DSPM) with real-time enforcement (DLP) to protect data whether it is stored, in use, or in transit. The Senior Security professional works to discover, classify, and monitor sensitive data across cloud, on-premises, and hybrid environments, ensuring compliance with data protection regulations.

The incumbent will be part of the team directly identifying and eradicating risks to AlterDomus, partnering with the business counter parts to primarily rollout a DSPM platform, implement data tagging through business alignment, and to create and tune DLP policies in conjunction with the company’s risk profile.

Data Security Posture Management

Discover and classify sensitive data (e.g., PII, PHI, financial data) across all data stores, including databases, SaaS applications, and cloud storage.
Assess data risk based on factors such as sensitivity, location, user access, and potential attack paths.
Continuously monitor the data environment for vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, and non-compliant data handling practices.
Enforce the Principle of Least Privilege by analyzing and managing data access permissions and entitlements to minimize the attack surface.
Remediate identified data risks by automating or directing actions, such as adjusting permissions, quarantining critical assets, or encrypting information.
Provide visibility into the data security landscape by creating reports and dashboards for stakeholders.

Data Loss Prevention

Develop, configure, and maintain DLP policies and rules across various channels, including email, web, endpoints, and cloud applications.
Monitor DLP alerts and investigate potential data leakage incidents and policy violations.
Analyze DLP incidents to identify root causes and patterns of data exfiltration.
Perform tuning of DLP policies to reduce false positives and improve the accuracy of sensitive data detection.
Collaborate with incident response teams to contain and resolve data security incidents promptly.
Work with data owners and business units to understand their data handling needs and refine DLP policies accordingly.

Compliance and Strategy

Ensure the organization's data protection practices align with regulatory requirements, such as GDPR and DORA
Generate audit-ready reports and compliance assessments to demonstrate adherence to relevant standards.
Help define and contribute to the broader enterprise data protection strategy, considering the entire data lifecycle.
Educate employees and stakeholders on data security best practices to foster a security-conscious culture.
Stay up to date with emerging data security trends, threats, and technologies, including securing AI and LLM training data.

Your Qualifications

Education
: A bachelor's degree in computer science, information security, or a related field is typically required.

Experience
: Several years of hands-on experience working with DLP and DSPM technologies in an information security role.

Technical Skills

Experience with DSPM platforms (e.g., Wiz, Prisma Cloud, BigID).
Proficiency with enterprise DLP solutions (e.g., Microsoft Purview, Symantec, Forcepoint).
Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS and Azure.
Experience with SIEM tools for security event analysis.
Understanding of data encryption, access controls, and network protocols.
Strong analytical abilities, experience creating and improving security reports and experience with data analysis/analytics tools such as Excel and Power BI. Developing dashboards would be a plus.

Certifications
: Professional security certifications such as Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) or CompTIA Security+ are highly valued. Any other DSPM / DLP Certifications highly desired.

Soft Skills

The ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
A keen attention to detail and a vigilant, investigative mindset
Excellent organizational skills and the ability to work under pressure on multiple projects, balance competing priorities, and meet deadlines both when working alone and with others.
Self-motivated and able to complete projects with minimal supervision.
Ability to rapidly evaluate, research, learn, and apply advanced and emerging data security principles, theories, and concepts.
Positive attitude and outstanding, proactive problem-identification and problem-solving skills.
Strong interpersonal and project management skills, and the ability to collaborate with colleagues across the Enterprise and to work effectively in a matrixed, geographically distributed organization.

We are committed to supporting your development, advancing your career, and providing benefits that matter to you.

Our industry-leading Alter Domus Academy offers six learning zones for every stage of your career, with resources tailored to your ambitions and resources from LinkedIn Learning.

new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Tetra Tech is seeking an experienced Environmental Project Manager
to join our Environmental Investigation, and Remediation team in the Goshen, New York or Woodbridge, New Jersey area
.

This position is ideal for an environmental professional with a background in engineering, environmental science, geology, or a related technical discipline
who has strong technical and project management capabilities.

The successful candidate will manage environmental projects for private-sector industrial in northern New Jersey. We are particularly interested in candidates with strong technical backgrounds in soil assessment, groundwater fate and transport, non-aqueous phase liquids (NAPL), and environmental chemistry. In addition, candidates should have strong project management skills, including the ability to plan and manage the scope, schedule, and budget of multiple fast-paced environmental assessment and remediation projects.

Why Tetra Tech

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Your Impact

Tetra Tech is a leader in the environmental industry, providing strategic planning, consulting, engineering, investigation, remediation, and compliance support for private-sector, industrial, and public-sector clients.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to lead projects addressing complex environmental challenges across multiple media, including soil, groundwater, sediment, surface water, and air
. You will work directly with clients, regulatory agencies, technical teams, and subcontractors to develop practical solutions and successfully deliver projects.

Position Summary

Working alongside a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, geologists, designers, and technical specialists, you will manage environmental investigation, remediation, and related projects from initial scoping through completion.

The position will include responsibility for project scope, schedule, budget, technical quality, staffing, client communication, and financial performance
. Depending on the project, responsibilities may include interpreting federal, state, and local environmental regulations; directing site investigations and remediation activities; evaluating technical data and calculations; and overseeing preparation of reports, plans, cost estimates, permit applications, and other deliverables.

Much of the technical work may support the investigation and/or remediation of active and inactive NJDEP Site Remediation Program sites.

Essential Job Functions

The following duties are considered essential to the role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.

Manage environmental investigation, remediation, and related consulting projects.
Manage project planning, scope, schedules, budgets, staffing, subcontractors, deliverables, and financial performance.
Plan, develop, coordinate, and direct multidisciplinary project teams.
Interpret and apply applicable federal, state, and local environmental regulations.
Assess environmental conditions, potential impacts, regulatory requirements, and technical challenges.
Scope environmental investigations, remediation programs, compliance activities, and other technical projects.
Review and interpret site-specific technical data, calculations, laboratory results, reports, drawings, cost estimates, environmental permit applications, and permit terms and conditions.
Prepare and/or oversee preparation of technical reports, work plans, permit applications, specifications, cost estimates, and other project deliverables.
Provide technical leadership and sound professional judgment when addressing complex project issues.
Coordinate with regulatory agencies, clients, laboratories, subcontractors, and other project stakeholders.
Direct and review the work of engineers, scientists, geologists, field personnel, and other technical staff.
Maintain project quality through appropriate technical review and quality assurance/quality control procedures.
Collaborate with the senior technical team to develop site closure strategies.
Mentor and support the professional development of junior and mid-level staff.
Manage multiple projects, clients, deadlines, and priorities concurrently.
Prepare proposals, scopes of work, schedules, staffing plans, and cost estimates.
Participate in client meetings, presentations, and interviews.
Identify upcoming client needs and opportunities for additional work.
Conduct periodic field and site visits to support project delivery and maintain familiarity with project conditions.
Assist field team implementing planned projects.
Work at remediation sites, construction sites, and other locations where heavy equipment, contamination, or other environmental or physical hazards may be present.
Travel within northern New Jersey based on project and client needs.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, or a related environmental or technical discipline.
Minimum of 5 years of relevant environmental consulting experience, including experience in one or more of the following:
Environmental investigation and remediation.
Brownfield or contaminated site redevelopment.
Industrial or private-sector environmental consulting.
Demonstrated project management experience, including responsibility for project scope, budgets, schedules, staffing, and deliverables.
Experience communicating directly with clients and managing client expectations.
Working knowledge of applicable federal and state environmental regulations.
Experience managing or coordinating multidisciplinary technical teams.
Strong technical problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities.
Self-motivated and disciplined, with the ability to learn new software and work effectively both independently and collaboratively.
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to build productive relationships with clients, colleagues, regulators, and subcontractors.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Project.
Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to client and project sites as needed.
Possess or able to obtain a Transportation Worker Identification Card (TWIC) by hire date.

Preferred Qualifications

7–10+ years of environmental consulting experience with progressively increasing project and client management responsibility.
Professional Engineer (PE), Professional Geologist (PG), or other applicable professional certification or licensure.
Experience with New Jersey environmental regulations and regulatory programs.
Experience working with NJDEP.
Experience managing investigation and remediation projects involving soil, groundwater, sediment, vapor intrusion, or other environmental media.
Experience working with sites with intermingled contamination.
Experience supporting industrial and private-sector environmental clients.
Experience developing scopes, budgets, and fee estimates and managing project financial performance, including invoicing.
Demonstrated ability to mentor and develop junior technical staff.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate environmental assessment data and determine the next step in the remediation process.
Experience with Autodesk Civil 3D, GIS, or other relevant environmental or engineering software is a plus.

Physical Requirements

Regularly required to sit and work at a computer for extended periods, with occasional standing and walking within an office environment.
Occasionally required to lift or move up to 10 lbs., with infrequent lifting of up to 25 lbs.
Requires use of hands for typing, handling materials, and operating office and field equipment.
Vision abilities include close vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
May travel to field sites, generally approximately 10–30% of the time, depending on project and client needs.
Field assignments may involve walking on uneven terrain and working around active construction, remediation, landfill, or industrial operations.
When in the field, must be able to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including a respirator when required, and meet applicable medical clearance requirements.

Work Environment / Environmental Factors

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those encountered while performing the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made.

Office-based work typically involves low hazard exposure, though noise levels may vary depending on nearby activities or equipment.
Outdoor project work may involve exposure to heat, cold, precipitation, uneven terrain, heavy equipment, physical hazards, and potential chemical or environmental hazards.
Appropriate PPE, including hearing protection and respiratory protection where applicable, may be required.
Travel between project sites, client locations, and Tetra Tech offices may be required, with employees expected to operate vehicles safely under varying weather, traffic, and environmental conditions.

Additional Information

This position will be based near Tetra Tech’s Goshen, New York or Woodbridge, New Jersey office.
A hybrid work arrangement may be available based on project, client, and team needs, with the expectation that the employee will be available for in-person client meetings, office collaboration, and project site visits as needed.
Regional travel throughout New York, New Jersey, and surrounding areas may be required.
Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future. Tetra Tech SWE will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work visa status for this opportunity (no sponsorship is available for H-1B, L-1, TN, O-1, E-3, H-1B1, F-1, J-1, OPT, CPT or any other employment-based visa).

Pay:

new_jobs.title: Environmental Remediation Project Manager/Office Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

This Opportunity

WSP has an exciting career opportunity for an Environmental Remediation Project Manager/Office Manager
to join our Rifle, CO
team. Scope of this role includes remedial design, field investigations, contaminated site management, data analysis and team oversight. This role will work closely with contaminated site portfolio leads and ensure the correct delivery of projects within the oil and gas industry, as well as overseeing the Rifle office on a day-to-day basis, overseeing staff and assisting with monitoring progress on contractor submittals, requests for Information, information bulletins, change/field Orders. This role would report to the North Mountain Site Investigation and Remediation (SIR) Service Line lead and be able to draw on expertise and resources in the SIR team throughout Colorado and the West.

Will have the opportunity to be involved in projects with our Earth & Environment Team and be a part of a growing organization that meets our client’s objectives and solves their challenges.

Are you looking for an exciting career opportunity where you can put your skills and talents to work with an established engineering consulting firm that values its employees’ enthusiasm and technical contributions? Do you enjoy managing projects and bringing in new projects? We encourage you to apply for this opportunity. We provide the atmosphere to allow individuals to grow their career. We’d love you to join our team of friendly, hard-working, dedicated and collaborative professionals. Our ideal candidate is seeking challenging work and is committed to quality.

Rifle, Colorado is a small town located on the beautiful Western Slope of Colorado, and centrally located 30 minutes west of Glenwood Springs; 1 hour northeast of Grand Junction, CO; 90 minutes northwest of Aspen, CO; 2 hours west of Breckenridge, CO and 3 hours west of Denver, CO.

Located directly on the Colorado River and near some of Colorado’s most popular tourist destinations, Rifle is the ideal location for adventure seekers. Residents enjoy skiing, fly fishing, hiking, camping, rafting, kayaking, and mountain biking all located right out your backdoor. Rifle Mountain Park (popular with rock climbers) is located 16 miles north of Rifle and Rifle Falls, Rifle Gap and Harvey Gap state parks are close by. There is access to BLM areas Hubbard Mesa Open Area, Rifle Arch and the Roan Plateau. The Rifle Creek Golf Course is 6 miles north of the center of Rifle.

Your Impact

Assist Senior Project Managers with their duties as necessary.
Coordinate weekly scheduling meetings.
Assist project Teams with multiple projects as requested.
Provide support to other staff on processes and requirements, monitor contract compliance, participate in the development of contracts.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Manage/oversee projects under the client’s Terms and Conditions which have been negotiated prior.
Support field staff collecting soil, groundwater and air samples for field and/or laboratory analyses.
Assisting and reviewing in the creation of detailed maps, lithologic logs and cross sections gathering, tabulating and analyzing data.
Preparing and reviewing proposals, cost estimates and technical reports for regulatory agencies submittal.
Oversee the team operating and maintaining field equipment and instrumentation.
Understand federal and state rules and regulations regarding environmental permitting compliance and remediation.
Provide senior-level expertise and technical guidance on complex regulatory projects.
Lead and mentor geologists, engineers and environmental scientists, guiding junior staff.
Prepare technical and Forms reports related for the Energy and Carbon Management Commission, Wyoming Oil and Gas Conservation Commission and Utah Department of Oil, Gas and Mining.
Takes projects from original discovery through final remediation.
Oversee various moderately-complex projects without the oversight of a Senior Project Manager and minimal oversight from technical teams.
Responsible for assembling project/task teams and assigning individual responsibilities, identifying appropriate resources needed. Given the complexity of the project, these teams could be larger, multi-disciplinary, and may reside in various states.
Develop the project scope and objectives, as well as clarify the role and function of each team member to effectively coordinate the activities of the team.
Identify, monitor, and mitigate risk on projects where the client may not have a full understanding of the project risks.
Take lead in development of proposals in collaboration with others.
Plan the execution of the project and monitor performance according to the project execution plan and the contract terms and conditions.
Manage project closure aspects ensuring correct project documentation.
Ensure project team (including sub-consultants/contractors) have understood and continually reassess the HSSE requirements of the project.
Develop and ensure adherence to the project schedule.
Supervise change request activities by appropriately addressing anticipated scope changes as they evolve and can advise others on scope change.
Assess and predict the possible impacts of schedule changes and the time management outcomes for future project impacts.
Develop a multi-disciplinary project budget and interact with subcontractors to develop the project budget.
Assign project budgets to task leaders and manage their performance.
Ensure compliance with client invoicing requirements and timely payment.
Will travel to project sites mostly in western Colorado and surrounding states. Approximately 10% overnight travel.

Who You Are

Required Qualifications

BS degree in Engineering, Geology, Environmental Science, or related discipline; PG or PE license preferred.
Minimum of 7 -10+ years of environmental consulting and/or project management experience.
Demonstrated experience with project financial tracking, and change management related to scopes of work.CAD, Civil 3D®, ArcGIS experience a plus
Expertise in project planning, numerical tracking and analysis (e.g., using MS Excel or similar programs).
Highly organized, adaptable, a developing leader and calm under pressure.
Experience in managing multi-discipline teams.
Effective interpersonal and communication skills when interacting with others, expressing ideas effectively and professionally to a scientific and non-scientific audience.
Highly capable self-leadership with attention to detail, multi-tasking, and prioritization of responsibilities in a dynamic work environment.
Ability to work independently and provide guidance and leadership to junior team or project members, with strict adherence to QA/QC.
Proficiency with technical writing, office automation and communication software, technology, and tools.
Ability to assertively direct others in the field such as subcontracted drillers, excavation contractors, utility locators, and others to consistently complete tasks safely and efficiently.
Proven track record of upholding workplace safety and ability to abide by WSP’s health, safety and drug/alcohol and harassment policies.
Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek
Ability and willingness to travel to project sites mostly in western Colorado and surrounding states. Approximately 10% overnight travel.
Must pass drug test, background check and must have a satisfactory driving record in accordance with the Company's driving (MVR) policy.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional licensure/certification.
40-Hour OSHA Health & Safety Training (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120) preferred.

WSP Benefits

WSP provides a comprehensive suite of benefits focused on providing health and financial stability throughout the employee’s career. These benefits include coverage related to medical, dental, vision, disability, and life; retirement savings; paid sick leave; paid vacation (or other personal time); paid parental leave; and paid time off for purposes of bereavement, voting, and/or attendance at naturalization proceedings.

Expected Salary (Colorado only): $105,000 - $175,000

WSP USA is providing the compensation range that the company in good faith believes it might pay and/or offer for this position within the state of Colorado, based on the successful applicant’s education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities in addition to internal equity and specific geographic location. WSP USA reserves the right to ultimately pay more or less than the posted range and offer additional benefits and other compensation, depending on circumstances not related to an applicant’s sex or other status protected by local, state, and/or federal law.

new_jobs.title: Credit Strategy Analyst III
new_jobs.description:
Advanced Business Intelligence Skills (e.g. Developing and publishing complex reports via Power BI Desktop)
Creates and delivers comprehensive reporting and monitoring of the portfolio credit quality, operations and performance
Design and create analysis using programing of data and/or statistical software to assess and understand new credit risk trends
Undertakes quantitative analysis to support improvements to credit strategy and policy
Deliver data, reporting and analysis to support the Indirect business as needed
Proactively identifies opportunities to improve data and automate analytic processes
Conducts analysis of large datasets using descriptive and predictive analytic techniques to provide insights and recommendations

Understands and articulates the business case of business questions and the estimated value being delivered. Designs dashboards and analyses to be performed, and appropriate visualization and analytics tools to use. Identifies trends and patterns to address identified business questions and provide insights through reporting and data visualization techniques. Works with other data and analytics professionals to optimize, refine, automate and scale analysis into repeatable analytics solutions and decision support tools.

Builds various reporting dashboards using the most appropriate data extraction, data cleaning and data visualisation techniques.
Provides value through insights, reporting and data visualization techniques. Selects, configures and implements analytics solutions for consistency and repeatability.
Researches and applies continuous improvement in data visualization by identifying trends and patterns to transform raw data into actionable business insights.
Works with different teams, management and stakeholders to enhance the usability and aesthetic appeal of data analytics solutions deployed in the organization.
Translates business needs to technical specifications and evaluates existing data visualization systems in order to improve them.
Develops data visualizations of "large" amounts of data that facilitate the intuitive presentation of data to decision makers.
Documents data flow, systems and processes to improve the design, implementation and management of business/group processes.
Develops tools and delivers training programs for use of reporting tools and self-serve analytics by non-analytical end users; may include delivery of training to audiences.
Focus is primarily on business/group within BMO; may have broader, enterprise-wide focus.
Provides specialized consulting, analytical and technical support.
Exercises judgment to identify, diagnose, and solve problems within given rules.
Works independently and regularly handles non-routine situations.
Broader work or accountabilities may be assigned as needed.
Take measured risks while protecting the bank by applying our Risk Management Framework in the execution of your role, in line with our Risk Culture and within our approved Risk Appetite, making sound and risk informed decisions that align to business strategy, protect assets, and adhere to applicable policy documents (Frameworks, Policies, Standards, Procedures and Supporting documents), laws and regulations.

Qualifications:

Foundational level of proficiency:

Technical design optimization.
Decision Making.
Systems Thinking.

Intermediate level of proficiency:

SQL, PowerBI, Python
Data visualization.
Data storytelling.
Data mining.
Illustration.
Creative thinking.
Problem Solving.
Verbal & written communication skills.
Collaboration & team skills.
Analytical and problem solving skills.
Data driven decision making.

Advanced level of proficiency:

Insights design.
Insights development and reporting.
Typically between 5 - 7 years of relevant experience and post-secondary degree in related field of study or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Deep knowledge and technical proficiency gained through extensive education and business experience.

Salary:

$75,000.00 - $160,000.00

Pay Type:

Salaried

BMO Financial Group’s total compensation package will vary based on the pay type of the position and may include performance-based incentives, discretionary bonuses, as well as other perks and rewards. new_jobs.title: Procurement & IT Sourcing Operations Analyst, Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Leads procurement and sourcing operations and serves as key contact to evaluate suppliers and vendors.

If you have experience working with IT suppliers or vendors, supporting technology or business teams, participating in procurement or contracting activities, managing projects, or partnering with a variety of stakeholders, your background could be a great fit for Enterprise Supply Management.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys building relationships, understanding business needs, managing multiple priorities, and working collaboratively across teams.

Core Responsibilities

Leads low and medium complexity sourcing transactions based on assessment of business needs. Leads and facilitates discussions on relationship, cost, and capabilities with leadership and suppliers.
Drives engagements through defined sourcing processes, resolving issues and involving stakeholders as needed. Interfaces heavily with other Sourcing teams, business owners, and Legal & Risk partners for each transaction.
Participates in strategic vendor-related initiatives. Provides relationship and project management expertise. Coordinates multiple stakeholders for input and collaboration for procurement activities.
Interprets and communicates contract requirements, obligations, and risk exposures to key stakeholders, including sourcing professionals and business leaders.
Oversees contract review, approvals, and negotiations. Champions sourcing process compliance and educates key stakeholders about commercial, legal, policy, and other considerations in support of the negotiation process.
Identifies and executes value creation opportunities through supplier consolidation, demand management, benchmarking, process optimization, and innovation partnerships.
Ensures supplier and contract data is submitted or entered into management systems and databases. Proactively considers and suggests vendor alternatives and contract timelines.
Supports adherence to procurement policies and procedures.
Participates in special projects and performs other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications:

Three years or more of related work experience in a sourcing capacity.
At least one year of prior IT sourcing experience partnering with vendors negotiating software, hardware and networking needs.
Undergraduate degree or equivalent combination of training and experience.

Special Factors

Sponsorship

Vanguard is not offering visa sponsorship for this position.

About Vanguard

At Vanguard, we don't just have a mission—we're on a mission.

To work for the long-term financial wellbeing of our clients. To lead through product and services that transform our clients' lives. To learn and develop our skills as individuals and as a team. From Malvern to Melbourne, our mission drives us forward and inspires us to be our best.

How We Work

Vanguard has implemented a hybrid working model for the majority of our crew members, designed to capture the benefits of enhanced flexibility while enabling in-person learning, collaboration, and connection. We believe our mission-driven and highly collaborative culture is a critical enabler to support long-term client outcomes and enrich the employee experience.

Replacement

The Global Trade Compliance team operates across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions in close collaboration with Husky’s Legal department. The team defines, implements, and continuously improves processes and policies to ensure compliance with global export control, sanctions, and customs regulations.

As the Global Trade Compliance Program Manager, you will report to the Director, Global Trade Compliance & Customs and serve as the program lead for enterprise-wide trade compliance initiatives. This role will focus on managing global compliance projects, optimizing processes, and ensuring the successful integration of trade compliance requirements into Husky’s systems.

You will partner with cross-functional teams—including Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, Finance, and Sales—to strengthen Husky’s global trade compliance framework, enhance operational efficiency, and reduce compliance risk across all regions.

Key Responsibilities

Program and Project Management

Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of global trade compliance initiatives, including process optimization, technology integration, and system enhancements.

Manage the implementation of trade compliance modules within the ERP system to ensure alignment with global regulatory requirements.

Establish and maintain project governance, milestones, KPIs, and reporting mechanisms for trade compliance programs.

Coordinate global stakeholders to ensure timely completion of key deliverables and consistent global deployment of compliance practices.

Regulatory Compliance and Oversight

Stay current on international trade laws, import regulations/tariffs, export control regulations, and sanctions programs applicable to Husky’s business activities.

Translate complex regulatory requirements into actionable business processes and internal controls.

Collaborate with Engineering and Legal teams to establish export control measures and export authorization processes globally.

Monitor the effectiveness of trade compliance procedures and implement corrective actions as needed.

Classification, Licensing, and Documentation

Lead efforts to standardize global product classification processes, including export control, HTS, and country-of-origin determinations.

Develop and maintain processes for end-use/end-user certifications, license applications, and transaction due diligence.

Ensure accuracy and consistency in trade data, documentation, and system configurations supporting export and customs compliance.

Risk Management and Continuous Improvement

Conduct global risk assessments and audits to evaluate compliance performance and identify improvement opportunities.

Develop risk mitigation strategies to prevent export control or import customs violations.

Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging digital tools and automation to enhance compliance monitoring and reporting.

Support internal investigations and voluntary disclosures, when applicable.

Training, Communication, and Stakeholder Engagement

Develop and deliver global training programs to increase awareness of export control, sanctions, and customs requirements.

Promote a culture of compliance through proactive communication and cross-functional collaboration.

Partner with IT, Supply Chain, and Finance to ensure trade compliance considerations are embedded in business processes.

Provide input in communications with government authorities and external consultants regarding trade compliance projects and inquiries.

Required Experience & Education

10+ years of progressive experience in global trade compliance, covering export controls, customs, sanctions, and trade agreements.

Deep understanding of U.S., EU, and Canadian export control and sanctions laws, with additional experience in UK, Swiss, Chinese, and other jurisdictions considered an asset.

Proven track record in managing large-scale trade compliance or ERP integration projects within a multinational organization.

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, International Business, Law, Supply Chain, or related discipline; PMP or other project management certification preferred.

Strong analytical and organizational skills, with the ability to interpret complex regulations and translate them into practical business solutions.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, capable of influencing and engaging stakeholders across multiple levels and functions.

Demonstrated ability to lead change, manage competing priorities, and deliver results under tight deadlines in a global environment.

Accordingly, Husky TechnologiesTM conditions all offers of employment on satisfactory completion of background checks.

new_jobs.description:
Location:
TDA AGH — Station-Based

Employment Type:
Full-Time

Schedule:
Standard business hours with flexibility to support station operations, safety events, and incident response as needed.

General Purpose Of The Job

Safety is not a department at TDA AGH — it is a culture. As Safety and Security Manager, you play a hands-on role in supporting and sustaining that culture at the station level. Working closely with station management and the TDA Safety team, you will help monitor safety compliance, support incident reporting and investigations, coordinate safety training, and serve as a visible, approachable safety resource for frontline teams. You will be responsible for a region of stations and travel as needed to support multiple operations.

This role is ideal for someone who is detail-oriented, proactive, and genuinely passionate about keeping people safe. You do not need to have all the answers — but you do need to ask the right questions, follow through on every action item, and consistently model the safety-first behaviors TDA expects of everyone on the team.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Safety Compliance & Monitoring:

Support the Safety Management System (SMS) program by ensuring safety program elements are being carried out day-to-day.
Monitor station compliance with FAA, TSA, OSHA, IATA, and company safety standards; flag concerns to station management and the Safety team promptly.
Conduct routine safety walkthroughs, inspections, and risk assessments; identify hazards, document findings, and follow up on corrective actions.
Track and report safety and security trends at stations; escalate patterns or recurring issues to leadership.

Incident Reporting & Investigation Support

Assist station management in documenting and reporting safety incidents and accidents accurately and in a timely manner.
Enter and maintain incident records in the SMS management platform.
Support root cause analysis and help track corrective action items through closure.

Training & Safety Education

Coordinate and facilitate monthly station safety meetings and safety workshops.
Distribute and review safety educational materials; ensure all team members have access to current safety resources.
Support the delivery of required safety training through the Learning Management System (LMS); track completion and flag overdue items.
Serve as a visible safety presence — engage with frontline employees, answer safety questions, and reinforce safe behaviors in real time.

Administrative & Program Support

Ensure reporting and documentation requirements are complete and accurate for your stations.
Leverage data and Safety Performance Indicators (SPIs) to drive actions.
Complete all required training.
Report any safety hazard or incident immediately per TDA SMS protocols.
Other duties as assigned by station leadership or the Director of Safety and Security.

Required

REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS:

Experience in the aviation industry or a similarly regulated operational environment.
Basic understanding of FAA, TSA, and OSHA safety regulations as they apply to airport ground handling operations.
Experience with IATA ground handling requirements and ISAGO certification standards.
Strong attention to detail with the ability to document incidents, track action items, and maintain accurate records.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Comfortable facilitating group safety meetings and communicating safety information clearly to frontline employees.
Must be able to work on the ramp and in operational areas as part of safety inspections and walkthroughs.
Must be willing to travel 30%.
Must successfully complete a 10-year background check and pre-employment drug screening.
Must be legally authorized to work in the United States.

Preferred

Prior experience supporting a Safety Management System (SMS) program.
Experience with the ISAGO standards and certification requirements.
Experience using a Learning Management System (LMS) for training coordination.
OSHA 10-hour General Industry certification or willingness to obtain.
Prior ramp, ground handling, or airline operations experience strongly valued.

Work Environment

This is a station-based role that combines office work with regular time on the ramp and in operational areas. Exposure to outdoor environments including extreme weather conditions, aircraft noise, fuel vapors, jet exhaust, and ground service equipment is expected. Personal protective equipment is required and provided when working in operational areas.

Physical Requirements

Must be able to navigate airport ramp and operational environments safely, including walking on uneven surfaces and working around active aircraft and ground equipment.
Prolonged periods of sitting and computer-based work when in an office or administrative setting.
Must be able to lift up to 25 lbs. occasionally.
Must have sufficient vision and physical ability to safely conduct site inspections and perform all essential functions of the position.

Key Competencies

Safety Mindset: Genuinely committed to keeping people safe; takes safety seriously every day, not just during audits or incidents.
Attention to Detail: Thorough and precise in documentation, inspections, and follow-up; nothing falls through the cracks.
Communication: Clearly conveys safety information to frontline employees and management; approachable, credible, and consistent.
Follow-Through: Tracks every action item, corrective measure, and training requirement to verified completion.
Proactive Awareness: Looks for hazards and trends before incidents occur; raises concerns early and constructively.
Collaboration: Works effectively with station managers, frontline teams, and the TDA Safety department; earns trust as a resource, not just a compliance checker.
Reliability & Accountability: Dependable and self-directed; takes ownership of the safety program at the station level with minimal supervision.
Adaptability: Adjusts priorities fluidly in response to operational changes, incidents, or evolving safety requirements.

Description

The Investment Operations Analyst
provides portfolio accounting, reconciliation, investment data, and operational support for the firm's investment management platform.

The Analyst is responsible for reconciling assigned portfolios, researching and resolving discrepancies, maintaining accurate investment data, developing operational reports and queries, and supporting projects and daily investment operations.

Working within an SEC-registered investment adviser environment, the position serves as an important component of the firm's operational control framework by helping ensure that positions, transactions, cash, cost basis, and other portfolio information are complete, accurate, and appropriately reconciled across portfolio accounting, trading, custodial, and related investment systems.

The Analyst works closely with the Director of Trading & Investment Operations, senior analysts, Portfolio Management, Trading, Investment Services, Technology, Compliance, custodians, and other business partners.

The position provides an opportunity to develop increasingly sophisticated expertise in portfolio accounting, trading operations, investment systems, reconciliation, data analysis, and operational risk management.

Essential Duties/Responsibilities To Be Performed With Or Without Accommodation.

Portfolio Accounting & Reconciliation

Perform daily and periodic reconciliation of assigned investment portfolios.
Reconcile portfolio:
Positions and holdings
Transactions and trade activity
Cash balances and activity
Cost basis and tax lots
Income and corporate actions
Security and other applicable investment data

Compare information across portfolio accounting, custodial, trading, and other investment systems.
Identify reconciliation breaks and research the underlying cause.
Resolve routine discrepancies independently and escalate more complex exceptions appropriately.
Coordinate with custodians and internal business partners to resolve outstanding items.
Ensure adjustments and corrections are accurately processed and appropriately documented.
Monitor unresolved exceptions through completion.

Trading & Investment Operations Support

Support daily investment-operating processes associated with trading, settlement, portfolio accounting, and reconciliation.
Research transaction, settlement, position, and cash discrepancies.
Assist with investigation and documentation of trade-related exceptions.
Support validation of investment activity between order-management, execution, custodial, and portfolio accounting systems.
Assist senior team members with operational reviews and exception management.
Provide timely operational support to Trading and Portfolio Management.
Develop an understanding of the complete investment lifecycle from portfolio decision through execution, settlement, accounting, and reconciliation.

Investment Data & Systems

Maintain and validate investment and portfolio data within applicable systems.
Develop proficiency with the firm's investment technology environment, which may include:
Advent/APX
Moxy
Genesis
Eze/ESE
Bloomberg
FactSet
Custodial platforms and interfaces
Reconciliation and reporting applications

Research system and data-feed discrepancies.
Assist with validation of information transmitted among investment systems.
Escalate system issues, unusual data conditions, and recurring exceptions.
Support testing associated with system upgrades, implementations, conversions, and enhancements.

Reporting, Queries & Analysis

Create and maintain queries and reports supporting investment operations.
Develop exception reports and analytical tools designed to identify discrepancies and improve controls.
Use Excel and other analytical tools to reconcile, organize, validate, and analyze investment data.
Assist in developing management and operational reporting.
Identify opportunities to automate recurring reports and manual processes.
Ensure reports and analyses are complete, accurate, and delivered within established deadlines.

Project Support & Process Improvement

Participate in investment operations, technology, data, and process-improvement projects.
Complete assigned project responsibilities in accordance with established milestones and deadlines.
Work with senior analysts and the Director of Trading & Investment Operations regarding project priorities and assignments.
Assist with documentation, data analysis, testing, validation, and implementation activities.
Identify opportunities to improve accuracy, efficiency, controls, and workflow.
Assist in developing and maintaining procedures, process documentation, and operational controls.
Communicate project status and potential issues proactively.

Operational Controls & Risk Management

Perform assigned responsibilities in accordance with established operating procedures and controls.
Maintain accurate documentation and audit trails supporting reconciliation and operational activity.
Identify and promptly escalate unusual transactions, unresolved exceptions, errors, or potential control deficiencies.
Assist with root-cause analysis of recurring operational issues.
Support efforts to reduce manual processing, errors, and operational risk.
Maintain appropriate segregation of duties within assigned processes.

SEC/RIA Compliance Support

Perform responsibilities consistent with the firm's fiduciary obligations, policies, procedures, and applicable SEC/RIA requirements.
Maintain complete and accurate records within assigned areas.
Support Compliance reviews, internal audits, regulatory examinations, and information requests as appropriate.
Promptly escalate potential compliance or operational concerns.
Maintain confidentiality and appropriate security of client, portfolio, and investment information.

Internal Business Partnership

Provide responsive daily support to Trading, Portfolio Management, Investment Services, and other internal business partners.
Research and respond to operational questions within the Analyst's area of responsibility.
Communicate the status of open items, exceptions, and resolution efforts clearly and proactively.
Develop productive working relationships across the investment organization.
Provide accurate and timely information to internal stakeholders.

Requirements

Education & Experience

Required

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or related discipline, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
Basic knowledge of investments, securities, financial markets, or portfolio accounting.
Demonstrated analytical and quantitative aptitude.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications.
Ability to work accurately with detailed financial and investment data.

Preferred

1–3 years of experience in investment operations, asset management, wealth management, trust, custody, brokerage, fund accounting, portfolio accounting, or financial services.
Experience performing financial or investment reconciliations.
Exposure to Advent/APX or comparable portfolio accounting platforms.
Exposure to Moxy, Genesis, Eze, Bloomberg, FactSet, custodial systems, or similar investment technology.
Experience developing queries, reports, or analytical tools.
Experience working within an SEC-registered investment adviser or other regulated financial-services environment.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Working knowledge of investments and financial markets with the ability to develop more advanced expertise.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
Ability to investigate discrepancies systematically and follow issues through resolution.
Ability to learn sophisticated investment systems and understand relationships among data sources.
Strong organizational and time-management skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and recurring deadlines.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently within established parameters and collaboratively within a team.
Intellectual curiosity and willingness to develop deeper technical and investment expertise.

Core Competencies

Accuracy & Quality
— Produces reliable work and recognizes the financial and operational importance of accurate portfolio information.

Analytical Thinking
— Uses data and structured analysis to investigate and resolve discrepancies.

Technical Aptitude
— Learns investment systems, data structures, and operational workflows quickly.

Accountability
— Takes ownership of assigned responsibilities and follows issues through resolution.

Risk Awareness
— Recognizes exceptions and understands when escalation is appropriate.

Continuous Improvement
— Looks for opportunities to improve processes, reporting, and controls.

Collaboration
— Works effectively with Trading, Portfolio Management, Investment Services, Technology, Compliance, custodians, and vendors.

Development Mindset
— Actively builds investment, systems, and operational expertise.

Key Measures of Success

Success in the role will include:

Accurate and timely completion of assigned portfolio reconciliations

Who We Are:

SOCi is the leader in AI-powered marketing solutions for multi-location businesses. With its proprietary Genius AI™ and suite of Genius Agents™, SOCi provides a first-of-its-kind, AI-powered digital workforce capable of handling the workload of 1,000 local marketers™, empowering brands to achieve unmatched digital visibility, strengthen customer engagement, and scale faster than ever before.

SOCi is recognized by Fast Company as one of the World's Most Innovative Companies, and is trusted by nearly 1,000 top brands—including Ford, Ace Hardware, Kumon, Liberty Tax, and more—to automate and optimize local marketing tasks across all locations. Founded in 2012 and backed by leading strategic investors, SOCi is transforming how multi-location brands manage and scale their marketing efforts. You can view our Awards and Accolades here!

About The Role

We are seeking a highly organized, analytical, and process-oriented Revenue Operations Analyst
to support our Customer Success, Sales, and Marketing organizations. This role will serve as a key operational partner across the customer lifecycle, helping teams operate efficiently through strong queue management, Salesforce administration and reporting, Customer Success operations, and cross-functional process management. The ideal candidate is comfortable working across multiple teams, can translate business needs into operational solutions, and has advanced Salesforce reporting skills. This person should be equally comfortable investigating an operational issue, building an executive-ready dashboard, coordinating a cancellation across multiple departments, and identifying opportunities to improve the underlying process.

Key Responsibilities

Revenue Operations Queue Management

Own the day-to-day management of the Revenue Operations request queue.
Review and triage incoming cases, determine priority and appropriate ownership, and route requests to the correct Revenue Operations team member or functional owner.
Manage assigned cases from intake through resolution, ensuring timely communication and appropriate follow-up with stakeholders.
Monitor queue health, aging, volume, and resolution times to ensure requests are addressed within established service-level expectations.
Identify recurring requests and issues that may indicate opportunities for process improvement, automation, documentation, or enablement.
Maintain clear documentation of case resolutions and operational changes.

Customer Success Operations

Serve as a primary Revenue Operations point of contact and operational partner for the Customer Success organization.
Partner with Customer Success leaders and team members to understand business requirements and translate them into scalable processes, reporting, and system improvements.
Support changes and enhancements to Salesforce and other Revenue Operations tools used by Customer Success.
Partner closely with Customer Success Enablement to ensure alignment and understanding of processes, tools, documentation, and enablement assets impacted by operational changes.
Help document and standardize Customer Success operational processes and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and scalability.
Support testing and quality assurance for system, workflow, and process changes before deployment.

Cancellation & Offboarding Operations

Manage and oversee the end-to-end customer cancellation process.
Coordinate across Customer Success, Implementation/Offboarding, Billing, Finance, and other stakeholders to ensure cancellations are processed accurately and on time.
Perform quality assurance throughout the cancellation process to ensure required information is complete, systems are updated appropriately, and downstream teams receive the information they need.
Identify and resolve discrepancies or process gaps that could impact customer offboarding, billing, reporting, or revenue data.
Maintain documentation and controls to ensure a consistent and auditable cancellation process.
Analyze cancellation trends and surface insights or recurring operational issues to Revenue Operations and Customer Success leadership.

Reporting & Analytics

Develop and maintain Salesforce reports and dashboards supporting Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, and Revenue Operations.
Partner with business stakeholders to understand reporting requirements and translate them into accurate, actionable reporting.
Provide Clari and CAP reporting to Customer Success leadership as needed.
Build recurring and ad hoc reporting to support leadership decision-making and operational reviews.
Perform quality assurance and validation of reporting to ensure data accuracy and consistency.
Investigate discrepancies across Salesforce and other revenue systems and partner with appropriate teams to resolve data issues.
Help establish consistent definitions and reporting methodologies for key revenue and customer metrics.

Salesforce & Data Management

Serve as a Salesforce reporting subject matter expert within Revenue Operations.
Build and maintain advanced Salesforce reports, dashboards, report types, filters, formulas, and related reporting solutions.
Support data quality initiatives by identifying incomplete, inconsistent, or inaccurate CRM data.
Partner with Revenue Operations and system administrators to recommend improvements to Salesforce fields, workflows, processes, and reporting structures.
Assist with user acceptance testing and quality assurance for Salesforce enhancements.
Help maintain documentation related to Salesforce processes, reporting definitions, and operational workflows.

Process Improvement & Operational Excellence

Identify opportunities to streamline manual processes and improve operational efficiency.
Document current-state and future-state processes, requirements, and standard operating procedures.
Partner cross-functionally to implement process improvements and measure their effectiveness.
Look for opportunities to reduce repetitive requests through automation, self-service reporting, documentation, and enablement.
Maintain strong attention to detail while balancing multiple requests, projects, and priorities.

Qualifications

2+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Customer Success Operations, Business Operations, or a related analytical/operational role.
Strong Salesforce experience with an advanced understanding of reports and dashboards.
Experience working with CRM data and translating business requirements into reporting or operational solutions.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to investigate data, identify trends, and communicate findings clearly.
Strong project and process management skills with the ability to manage work from intake through completion.
Excellent attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy and quality assurance.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively with stakeholders across multiple departments.
Ability to prioritize competing requests and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment.
Comfortable identifying problems, recommending solutions, and taking ownership through resolution.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting a SaaS or recurring-revenue business.
Experience supporting Customer Success operations and customer lifecycle processes.
Experience with Clari or similar revenue intelligence/forecasting platforms.
Experience with ticketing or case-management workflows.
Experience working with customer cancellation, offboarding, billing, or renewal processes.
Experience with data visualization or business intelligence tools.
Familiarity with revenue metrics including ARR, churn, retention, renewals, pipeline, and forecast reporting.
Experience identifying opportunities for workflow automation and operational scale.

Our collaborative, dynamic culture allows our teams to work cross-functionally and optimize productivity. We are a fast-paced, agile environment where thought leadership and input are encouraged. new_jobs.title: Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
At the MBTA, we envision a thriving region enabled by a best-in-class transit system. Our mission is to serve the public by providing safe, reliable, and accessible transportation. MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

The Data Analyst (TID) is part of the Transit Technology team within the Transformation & Technology Department. The Transit Technology team is responsible for designing, building, and maintaining dispatching systems and other technology tools that enable MBTA Operations division to deliver safer, more efficient, and more reliable transit services. This role will work closely with Transit Tech product teams to measure and monitor the success of technology products and initiatives as part of outcome-driven technology delivery.

The Data Analyst (TID) will empower stakeholders to make data-driven decisions and create a culture of continuous improvement. The position will collect, clean, and validate data, perform statistical analyses using modern data analysis and visualization tools, communicate findings, and write technical documentation. The Data Analyst will collaborate with other team members to share knowledge, provide cross-training, and jointly support cross-divisional projects.

Duties & Responsibilities

Design dashboards, visualizations, graphs, charts, and tools that clearly communicate outcomes, findings, and trends of Operations data.
Proactively build and maintain positive and effective relationships with Departments. Work with Departments to analyze results, forecast current and future needs, assess performance, and evaluate strategic opportunities.
Communicate with and present to executive leadership project results and findings.
Gather, analyze, and interpret operational data using a combination of SQL, Excel, Python and/or relevant modern data analysis tools.
Perform quality control on data inputs, calculations, algorithms, and model outputs, and investigate associated data gaps or inconsistencies.
Develop tools to facilitate the automation and dissemination of analyses.
Prepare scheduled and ad-hoc reports, slideshows, and other visual reports incorporating narratives and graphic data, for both online and print formats.
Manage timelines, project milestones, and communications with internal and external partners.
Respond to each inquiry, whether from a customer, vendor, or coworker, in a courteous and professional manner consistent with the Authority’s quality standard.
Work directly with Operations Leadership to identify the needs specific to the assigned division.
Collaborate with other Analysts on the knowledge sharing, cross-training, and joint support of cross-division projects.
Perform all other duties and projects that may be assigned.

Additional responsibilities may include a focus on one or more departments or locations. See applicable addendum for department or location specific functions.

Supervision

No direct reports.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications

A Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in business, finance, economics, computer science, data science, urban planning, engineering, or a related field.
Two (2) years of experience in data science, business analytics, business intelligence, quantitative analysis, or other related fields.
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. As part of the interview process, an Excel assessment may be required.
Experience in at least one approach to advanced data analysis (e.g., SQL, Python, R, SPSS, GIS, or other).
Ability to learn quickly, take direction, work independently, and use creative and collaborative approaches to resolve issues.
Effective organizational, analytical, multi-tasking, and time management skills.
Effective written and verbal communication skills.
Possess strong statistics and data fundamentals.
The ability to work effectively with a diverse workforce.

Preferred Experience & Skills

Experience with relational databases (e.g., Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Oracle), including writing queries to obtain and manipulate data.
Experience with Python, Excel VBA, or other programming languages, and/or data management and statistical analysis tools (R, SPSS, STATA, SAS, etc.).
Experience with Tableau or other visualization software.
Familiarity with transportation planning and transit systems, particularly the MBTA subway and bus network

Substitutions

A High School Diploma or GED with an additional seven (7) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
An associate degree from an accredited institution and an additional three (3) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
A master’s degree in a related subject substitute for two (2) years of general experience.
A nationally recognized certification, or statewide/professional certification in a related field substitutes for one year of experience.

Job Conditions

Ability to effectively read, comprehend, communicate, and respond to instructions, orders, signs, notices, inquiries, etc. in English.
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age, except if participating in an approved high school internship / co-op program.
Ability to commute to assigned work locations in the Boston, MA metro area, as required by the role.
Ability to provide internal and external customers with courteous and professional experiences.
Ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a diverse workforce team (or supervise, if required).
Ability to uphold the rights and interests of the MBTA while building and maintaining effective relationships with employees and co-workers.
Ability to adhere to rules, regulations, collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and policies of the MBTA, including the EEO, anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, and anti-retaliation policies.
Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years immediately prior to the closing date of this posting (unless if current student or recent graduate), including overall employment, job performance, discipline, and safety records (infractions and/or offenses occurring after the closing of the posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).
Ability to pass a Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check, comprehensive background screening, and / or medical Clinic screening, potentially including physical examination and drug and alcohol screenings.
Ability to work all shifts and / or locations assigned, directed, or necessary for this position, including (for some transit / operations roles) up to twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week as necessary to accommodate severe weather conditions, emergencies, or any other circumstances that may potentially impact service or the safety of service.
Intern / co-op staff must be enrolled full or part-time in an accredited educational program and maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 2.5 for the entire duration of the internship / co-op. Additionally, interns / co-ops must have valid work authorization and U.S. Social Security Number prior to starting pre-employment screenings / pre-boarding, working in their positions, and throughout the duration of their program.

Description

The Rapid & Rural Logistics (R2L) team is seeking a strategic Program Manager to lead AI Enablement across our high-growth operational businesses. R2L owns end-to-end customer fulfillment aspects including supply chain planning, operations, central programs, delivery, and technology. This role will design and implement frameworks that democratize AI capabilities, enabling teams to leverage AI to drive operational excellence through intelligent automation. This role requires a strategic leader who can balance executive stakeholder management with cross-functional coordination, change management expertise with technical fluency, and strategic thinking with pragmatic execution.

You will build the capability development programs, enablement frameworks, and partnership mechanisms that transform R2L employees into AI-capable problem solvers who can build self-help tools and prototypes using their business knowledge. This includes creating structured learning pathways that enable employees to graduate from foundational AI skills to active problem-solving, facilitating partnerships with Tech teams to scale prototypes into production solutions, and measuring success by how many employees are actively solving business problems with AI.

Key job responsibilities

Translate the AI enablement vision into executable roadmaps, designing programs that transform employees into AI-capable problem solvers through scalable playbooks, role-based pathways (AI Explorer, Practitioner, Champion), and an AI Champions network that fosters a culture of AI-first thinking
Design and execute programs that transform R2L employees into AI-capable problem solvers who can build self-help tools and prototypes using their business knowledge

Drive adoption of AI tools through internal communications, workshops, and an AI Champions network to foster a culture of AI-first thinking and active problem-solving
Partner with Tech teams, and other stakeholders to facilitate partnerships, scale prototypes into production solutions, and integrate AI into existing workflows

Define and track KPIs for AI adoption (training completion, active tool usage, prototypes developed, solutions scaled), productivity gains, and ROI to provide transparency to senior leadership

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Oncology Care Pathways
new_jobs.description:
About Viz.ai

Viz.ai is the leader in building and deploying AI-powered Care Pathways and helping doctors do their work. The Viz Platform is deployed in 2,000 hospitals across the United States and trusted by many of the leading life sciences companies. The platform uniquely combines real-time, multimodal clinical data with deep clinician engagement to detect disease earlier, coordinate care teams, and help ensure patients receive the right treatment faster. Viz.ai was the first company to be awarded CMS reimbursement for AI and is ranked the #1 Healthcare AI Platform by hospitals and health systems in the Black Book Research survey. For more information, visit Viz.ai.

The Role

We're looking for an Oncology Program Manager to support the execution of Viz's oncology care pathways — and to own the operating system that lets them scale.

Working alongside our care pathway leads, you'll help get sites live, train and onboard the clinicians who use the product, build durable relationships across the oncology and urology community, and serve as the clinical voice for Sales and Customer Success. You'll also do something new for us: operate oncology as a program . That means one source of truth for site status and milestones, a clear operating rhythm across functions, clean handoffs, and escalation paths that work without requiring an executive in the room.

Oncology at Viz has real clinical momentum and real customer demand. It is also complicated by multiple dependencies and processes that need to get simpler — and success in this role depends on close collaboration with Product, Sales, Customer Success, Implementation, and Finance.

The ideal candidate combines the field credibility of a care pathway lead with the discipline of a strong program manager, and the instincts of someone who has worked inside an AI-native company and knows how fast the ground moves.

What You'll Own

Care Pathway Execution

Enable and coordinate oncology care pathway delivery from contract execution through technical go-live, clinical activation, and sustained use — through a combination of direct execution and a focus on process improvement.
Develop tight processes for planning, anticipating, and managing the site-side work that determines whether a site goes live on time: IT and EHR dependencies, IRB and research contracting, configuration, data validation, and clinical champion sign-off.
Work with clinical sales, demand generation, and marketing to build per-site activation plans and the pipeline behind them, so we're consistently carrying enough sites to hit commitments even when individual accounts slip.
Partner with Finance and our life sciences teams on the milestone implications of go-live timing, so the numbers people see reflect reality.

Clinician Onboarding, Training, and Adoption

Design and deliver onboarding and training for oncologists, urologists, APPs, navigators, and pharmacists at each activating site.
Build reusable training assets — quick-start guides, role-based walkthroughs, refresher sessions — so the tenth site is faster than the first rather than the same.
Monitor early usage after go-live and intervene before disengagement sets in, closing the loop with Product and Clinical AI on issues that surface in the field.

Relationships and Clinical Voice

Build and hold trusted relationships with clinical champions, service line leaders, and administrators at community urology networks, academic cancer centers, and large IDNs.
Serve as a site's point of contact through activation and early adoption, and know when to pull in colleagues rather than absorbing it alone.
Represent Viz at oncology and urology society meetings.
Support Sales and Customer Success in customer conversations, demos, and objection handling with credible, clinically grounded answers.
Contribute clinical input into product direction — workflow realities, guideline changes, what clinicians will and will not tolerate — in close partnership with Product, who owns requirements and roadmap.

Oncology Program Management

Establish a single, maintained source of truth for oncology: site status, milestones, owners, blockers, and dates. One place, current, that anyone from Sales to Finance to R&D can read without asking.
Establish clean interfaces, handoffs, and escalation paths across Clinical, Product, Engineering, Implementation, Sales, CS, Contracting, and Finance, with named owners.
Bring order to how oncology communicates, so technical and product issues have one home and site-level engagement and training have another — and hold that line as new work starts.
Build the reporting leadership and partners actually need, in collaboration with our platform and value demonstration teams.

Qualifications

5+ years in oncology or urology — clinical operations, care pathways, clinical program management, field medical, implementation, or customer-facing clinical roles — with real fluency in how cancer care is actually delivered.
Direct experience in the community urology or community oncology setting, including how these practices and networks make decisions, buy, and adopt new workflow technology.
Demonstrated multi-site, multi-stakeholder program or project management with hard deadlines — you're the person who keeps the tracker honest.
Experience at an AI-native or high-growth health technology company, with comfort in the pace, ambiguity, and frequent replanning that comes with it.
A track record of getting clinical sites live — and of closing the gap between "technically live" and "clinicians are using it."
Strong clinical fluency and credibility with oncologists and urologists, whether or not you hold a clinical license.

A care pathway is not delivered when the technology is live. It is delivered when clinicians change what they do because of it.

We're looking for someone who finds that work interesting rather than beneath them, because it's the highest-leverage work we have in oncology right now.
